title: paged-kv-cache: block-manager allocator reuse, locality-aware pinning, and reuse heuristics
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: the paged KV cache has regressed under long-context multi-tenant workloads due to allocation churn and suboptimal pin placement across NUMA/GPU locality domains. This PR improves block allocator reuse, introduces locality-aware pinning heuristics, and tightens reuse TTLs to reduce cold-path allocations and reduce GPU memory fragmentation.

What this PR does (high level):
- Reuse allocator instances for short-lived allocations to avoid creating/destroying allocator metadata on hot paths. This reduces lock contention and per-request allocation overhead.
- Introduce locality-aware pinning: blocks are preferentially pinned to the same device/NUMA domain as the request route when affinity information is available. Falls back to global pinning when unavailable.
- Add configurable reuse heuristics and TTLs: tunable thresholds for reuse window, eviction scoring now weights locality and recent access frequency, and a short-path fast-evict for large one-off prompts.
- Expose metrics for allocator churn, pinned-block locality hits, and reuse hit-rate to help ops tune policies.
- Add tests and microbench harness changes; update changelog and docs snippet for tuning knobs.

Benchmarks: on our perf-canary long-context suite (seq_len=16k, multi-tenant mix), we see: median latency reduced ~9%, p95 latency reduced ~12%, and sustained throughput improvement of 10-18% depending on request mix. GPU memory fragmentation decreased (observed 8-14% reduction in usable fragmentation space) which reduces OOM noise on heavy workloads.

Compatibility: this change is fully backward compatible at the API level; it introduces new config knobs with sensible defaults. We also added a runtime flag to force old allocator behavior for quick rollback.

Notes: there was an initial CI flake in perf-canary (timeout on perf job) which required a config bump in the harness; all checks passed after re-run. See review conversation for tradeoffs considered about cross-device pin migration and eviction fairness.

b4d9e11: perf(kv_cache): locality-aware pinning and affinity API

d9f6b4e: tests: add kv cache microbench and integration tests; update docs
review_conversation: Mary Johnson: Please add a brief note on how pin locality behaves when requests are routed across GPUs; is there a migration strategy?

Evan Park: We intentionally avoid cross-device migration to keep the fast path lock-free. Migration was considered but introduced additional synchronization and increased p95 in local experiments. We added a config flag for forced migration for experiments (disabled by default).
Diego Morales: Can you add metrics for allocator churn and a tracing span so we can correlate with SLO regressions?
Evan Park: Added allocator_churn metric and a tracing span around allocation hot path (commits a8f3c2e / c2a7ff0).
Hannah Lee: The reuse TTL default looks aggressive (100ms) — ops may want longer for multi-process bursts. Can we make it configurable and document recommended values?
Evan Park: TTL is now configurable via KV_CACHE_REUSE_TTL_MS with default 100ms; added docs and examples.
release_notes: Improved paged KV cache block manager: allocator reuse, locality-aware pinning, reuse TTLs and metrics. Expect lower latency and better throughput for long-context workloads; new tuning knobs available.
